title: Go loop refuses to double-start
notes: history.jsonl shows two loop_started events 42 seconds apart on 2026-08-22 (pids 56941 and 59762), so two loops can run at once and race on task claims. Make go-loop.sh check status.json on startup: if it records a pid that is still alive, exit with a clear message instead of starting a second loop. A stale pid (process gone) is fine to take over. Acceptance: starting the loop twice leaves exactly one running loop and the second invocation explains why it declined.

log.note: added queue.mjs 'alive' subcommand (prints live loop pid or 'no' via loopAlive) and a startup guard in go-loop.sh: before touching status/history it reads the recorded pid; if that process is alive AND its command matches go-loop (pid-reuse guard), it declines with a clear message and exit 1. Stale/dead/recycled pids are taken over.

verified live: second invocation while pid 59762 runs declined with message + exit 1, appended nothing to history.jsonl, left the original loop running. Dead pid, null pid, and alive-but-unrelated pid (tail -f) all correctly allow startup. Scripts/test.sh green (863 tests).

go-loop.sh now declines to start when status.json's pid is a live go-loop process (pid-reuse safe); verified by real double-start against the running loop (declined, exit 1, no history event) and stale-pid takeover checks. New queue.mjs 'alive' subcommand backs the check.
